summary: Feed s161_triple to NDR is degraded: 3 faults detected. VLAN 20 is missing (50% untagged), 16.4% duplicates inflate traffic, and 92.9% encrypted share exceeds 90% NDR tolerance. Bidirectional flow and packet delivery are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags or filtering VLAN 20 upstream. 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 never appears despite NDR requiring VLANs 10 and 20, indicating trunk not forwarding VLAN 20 or broker set to strip tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR has zero visibility into VLAN 20 segment; detections, asset discovery and lateral movement coverage for that VLAN are blind.

recommended_fix.why: Restore VLAN 20 to the NDR and preserve 802.1Q tags through the broker so NDR can segment and detect per-VLAN correctly.

findings.root_cause: 16.4% duplicates (444/2709) indicates same packet delivered via multiple SPANs or broker aggregation without deduplication - classic SPAN duplication or looped TAP aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate flows, inflates flow counts and alerts, and can skew behavioral analytics and TCP reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication to deliver single copy of each packet to the 10G NDR port, restoring accurate counts and freeing capacity.

findings.root_cause: 92.9% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) exceeding NDR's 90% tolerance. Feed is predominantly opaque TLS with no decryption point before the NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection but cannot inspect encrypted payloads; threat detection degrades to metadata only and payload signatures are blind.

recommended_fix.why: Add selective SSL/TLS visibility/decryption before the NDR or feed decrypted copy to restore payload inspection while respecting privacy policy.
